patches.summary: Every scrape command persists into the local store, best-effort: airbnb_listing search/get, cheapest, compare, plan, and watch check write the scraped listing (and extracted host) via UpsertAirbnbListing/UpsertHostRecord, and write a dated price_snapshots row via InsertPriceSnapshot whenever a real positive price was scraped. Persistence is a side-effect that must never alter the live scrape result or surface an error: store-open failures, missing-id cards, and write errors are swallowed/stderr-warned.
patches.reason: The scrape commands call source/airbnb directly and print typed results; nothing they fetched was being persisted, so the store-backed readers (host portfolio, wishlist diff) and InsertPriceSnapshot/UpsertHostRecord stayed orphaned with zero callers. Airbnb's SSR returns search cards that sometimes lack a stable id (UpsertAirbnbListing rejects empty-id with 'missing id for airbnb_listing'), and frequently returns no bookable total for given dates (airbnbTotals -> 0). Persistence is therefore guarded: skip listings with empty id, and write a price snapshot ONLY when total > 0 so an unavailable price never becomes a phantom $0 row polluting price history. A regen must keep persistence best-effort and keep the price>0 snapshot guard.
patches.validated_outcome: go build/vet/test green. Unit tests assert a listing row lands and an empty-id card is skipped without error; a positive total writes one snapshot while zero/negative totals and empty ids write none. Live smoke: one airbnb_listing search --rate-limit 0.3 into an isolated store populated the resources + airbnb_listing tables.

patches.summary: Default `sync` (no --resources) re-scrapes what the store already knows — every watchlist entry (with its saved dates) and every previously-scraped airbnb_listing, de-duplicated by URL — and persists fresh price snapshots via the same best-effort scrape-persist path. An empty store is reported honestly (sync_warning reason=empty_store) with NO network call, never a 404. The authenticated Airbnb wishlist sync is preserved as an explicitly opt-in, auth-gated resource: `sync --resources airbnb_wishlist` routes to airbnb.WishlistList behind 'auth login --chrome' and surfaces an auth error (not a 404) when cookies are missing. Any other explicitly-named resource still flows through the legacy API-mirror syncResource engine.
patches.reason: Airbnb has no public paginated collection, so the generated default (defaultSyncResources -> ['airbnb_wishlist'] -> syncResourcePath -> a GraphQL persisted-query path) 404s/auth-gates on every default run. A scraper's 'sync' must mean 'refresh what you've already seen', driving off store state (ListWatchlist + the airbnb_listing table) rather than a remote cursor. The auth-gated wishlist path (airbnb.WishlistList, cookie jar) is real functionality and must NOT be deleted — it stays selectable and documented-as-requiring-auth. The legacy syncResource/syncResourcePath machinery is kept intact because the auto-refresh hook still uses it for the airbnb_wishlist read paths. A regen must keep the default as a store-driven re-scrape with an honest empty-store report, and keep the auth-gated wishlist resource selectable.
patches.validated_outcome: go build/vet/test green. collectScrapeTargets test: empty store yields zero targets; watchlist + known listings are gathered and de-duplicated by URL with watchlist dates winning. Live smoke: sync against an empty isolated store emitted sync_warning reason=empty_store and made no network call (exit 0); sync against a store seeded with one known listing re-scraped it and persisted a snapshot.

patches.summary: watch check treats a non-positive scraped price as 'no price data', never a drop: such items are recorded with hit=false, surfaced in a top-level no_price[] bucket (reason no_price_data), and NEVER trigger the exit-7 drop sentinel. Exit 7 fires only when a real positive price is at or below a positive max-price threshold. The decision lives in the pure helper classifyWatchPrice(price, maxPrice) -> (hasPrice, hit).
patches.reason: firstPlatformTotals returns 0 both for a genuinely-free listing and for one whose SSR price was unavailable for the dates, and cannot distinguish them. The old condition `price <= item.MaxPrice` was always true for price==0 against any positive threshold, so an unavailable price produced a false hit and a spurious exit 7 (the watch drop sentinel) on every cron run. Exit 7 is dual-purpose (genuine HTTP 429 AND the watch drop-hit success signal), so the guard must live in watch check where the watchlist intent is known; it must preserve real exit-7 drops while never firing on no-price. The output envelope is a top-level object ({"hits":[...],"no_price":[...]}) because --agent/--compact drops non-allowlisted fields from bare arrays.
patches.validated_outcome: go build/vet/test green. classifyWatchPrice table test: price 0 or negative => hasPrice=false, hit=false for any threshold (no exit 7); positive price hits only at/under a positive threshold. Live smoke confirmed watch check on a real listing returned an envelope with hits + no_price and exit 0 (no false exit 7).

patches.summary: `watch remove <listing-url-or-id>` deletes a watchlist entry, backed by store.DeleteWatchlistItem(listingURL) which DELETEs by the UNIQUE listing_url and returns the rows-affected count. A full listing URL is matched verbatim; a bare id is resolved to its stored URL by scanning the watchlist for a matching listing_id, so users can remove by the same id shown in `watch list`. Removing an absent listing is a not-found (exit 3), not a silent success.
patches.reason: The watchlist had add/list/check but no removal path, so a watched listing could never be taken off without editing the DB by hand. The delete keys on listing_url (the UNIQUE column) to hit exactly one row; the id-resolution step exists because the URL the user added and the bare room id are both natural identifiers and `watch list` surfaces the id. A regen must keep the delete method on the hand-written store/rental.go (next to the other watchlist mutators, under writeMu), not on generated store.go.
patches.validated_outcome: go build/vet/test green. Store test: seed one watchlist row, DeleteWatchlistItem returns 1 and COUNT drops to 0; deleting again returns 0 with no error. Live smoke: watch add then watch remove then watch list returned an empty watchlist.
